relations.note: Mnaseas makes Stymphalos the father of the human Stymphalides.
Mnaseas makes Ornis, whose name means Bird, their mother.

relations.myth: Heracles expels the birds with rattles
relations.note: Heracles drives the flock from Stymphalos using loud rattles.

relations.myth: Heracles attacks the flock with a sling
relations.note: Archaic vase art shows Heracles confronting sixteen waterbirds with a sling.
Heracles kills some birds and frightens the immense remaining flock away.

relations.myth: The sixth labor at Lake Stymphalis
relations.note: Heracles flushes the inaccessible birds with bronze clappers and shoots them.
Heracles kills the human Stymphalides after they refuse him hospitality.

relations.myth: Heracles kills the birds on Mars's island
relations.note: Hyginus relocates their destruction by Heracles to the island of Mars.

relations.myth: Athena supplies Heracles with bronze clappers
relations.note: Athena obtains Hephaestus's noisemakers and gives them to Heracles.
Athena appears beside Heracles in the monumentalized labor scene.

relations.myth: The bronze clappers used against the birds
relations.note: Hephaestus makes or possesses the noisemakers Athena gives Heracles.
The Black Sea flock inhabits Ares's island and is called his birds.
Later Roman tradition identifies the Stymphalian flock with Mars's nurslings.

relations.myth: Bird imagery at Artemis's Stymphalian sanctuary
relations.note: Bird figures and bird-legged maidens decorate her sanctuary, without a narrated encounter.

relations.myth: Medea's offering of a Stymphalian feather
relations.note: Medea offers Hecate a feather taken from a wounded Stymphalian bird.

relations.myth: Phineus advises noise against the island birds
relations.note: The prophetic adviser directs the Argonauts to repel the birds with noise.

relations.myth: The Argonauts repel the birds of Ares
relations.note: The Argonauts use shields, spears, shouting, and noise to drive them away.
One bird launches a sharp feather that wounds Oileus in the shoulder.
Clytius shoots down one member of the projectile-feathered flock.
The human Stymphalides welcome the Molionids while refusing Heracles hospitality.
